messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the 2245 kernel rollout we saw a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate on prod at ~10:12 UTC, +18% miss rate vs baseline. p95 generation latency climbed ~60ms for small requests.

dan: ugh. any obvious churn/eviction logs?

maria: yes — eviction rate for KV shards rose ~3x. stacktrace points at the new fused-attn kernel using different KV buffer alignment, which increases per-seq memory slightly. when workers hit memory threshold they evict more aggressively.

jon: can you paste the profiling snippet?

maria: sure — from the hot path: 
```
2026-02-18T10:11:58Z perf: kernel=fused-attn-v2 shard=kv-17 mem_used=12168MB mem_limit=12288MB evictions=27
2026-02-18T10:12:02Z perf: kernel=fused-attn-v2 batch_size=4 p50=24ms p95=142ms cache_hit_rate=68.4%
2026-02-18T10:12:02Z baseline: kernel=fused-attn-v1 batch_size=4 p50=20ms p95=82ms cache_hit_rate=86.2%
```

nidhi: interesting — hit-rate delta ~18 points lining up with the eviction spike. could be either the kernel memory footprint or subtle key canonicalization diffs due to system-prompt ordering change we shipped last week.

dan: we did land sys-prompt reordering in the same deploy window (small optimization in prompt builder). if order of tool fields changed that could alter tokenization and keys.

maria: i compared raw prompt fingerprints (sha1 of concatenated tokens) for a sample cohort: 99.97% match but 23k out of 8.2M requests had different fingerprints — those correlate strongly with misses.

jon: so two hypotheses: (A) small per-request memory increase -> extra evictions -> misses, (B) rare canonicalization changes -> different keys for some requests. both could be true. how to triage quickly?

maria: plan: 1) rollback kernel for a canary subset of workers (route 5% traffic to fused-attn-v1) 2) run A/B with pinned tokenizer v2 vs unpinned to see canonicalization impact 3) increase shard memory soft-threshold and observe eviction rate 4) synthetic warmup to prefill top prefixes for impacted routes.

jon: +1. For (1) we should measure cache hit-rate delta and p95 on the canary in the next 30m. deploy-bot can help route.

deploy-bot: routing change queued: 5% -> fused-attn-v1 canary. will apply in 2m. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

maria: added metrics query used for dashboards: 
```sql
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) AS t, avg(p95_ms) AS p95, avg(cache_hit_rate) as hit
FROM inference_metrics
WHERE model = 'redwood-llama-13b' AND route IN ('chat','completion')
GROUP BY t ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 60;
```

nidhi: also adding a quick checksum check in the warmup path to detect tokenizer-version churn. if checksum mismatch occurs, we log both token counts and raw prompt so we can inspect.

dan: what about batching heuristics interacting here? iirc newer kernel changed optimal batch packing and we bumped continuous-batching defaults. could be higher transient batch sizes causing larger KV per-worker caches.

maria: good point — we saw average batch_size jump from 3.9 -> 4.3 on some shards after rollout. batching + memory footprint could push a shard over the soft-limit more frequently.

jon: propose short experiments (each runs 30m A/B):
- E1: kernel v1 vs v2 routing 5/95 (isolate kernel effect)
- E2: tokenizer pin v2 vs unpinned (isolate canonicalization)
- E3: bump per-shard soft-memory by 10% (isolate eviction sensitivity)
- E4: synthetic warmup of top 500 prefixes on a sample of workers (test warmup efficacy)

maria: i'll kick off E1+E3 now. nidhi can you prepare the tokenizer pin experiment and checksum logging? jon can you coordinate the warmup job?

nidhi: on it — will add opt-in flag so we can test without full rollout. logging will include tokenized length and fingerprint.

jon: warmup job will use latest real traffic traces to pick top prefixes. plan: 10k warmup requests spread across boot cycle so it doesn't spike traffic. also will mark warmup traffic as low-priority so it doesn't affect SLOs.

maria: after 15m of canary we already see eviction rate down ~60% on canary and cache_hit_rate up to 85% on those workers. p95 also dropped ~45ms. promising.

dan: nice! any sign tokenizer pin affecting those specific miss cases?

maria: not yet — misses reduced primarily by fewer evictions in the canary. still want to run E2 to rule out the small correlated set of fingerprint diffs.

nidhi: started E2 in a small cohort (1%). early logs show the checksum mismatch events are almost always related to tool field ordering when tool list is empty vs omitted (ugh). i have a patch proposal to normalize tool field emission (always emit empty array).

jon: sounds good — can we A/B that normalization quickly? low risk.

maria: yep, patch looks safe. if we normalize tool list serialization, those 23k mismatches should go away. combine that with kernel rollback → should restore full hit-rate.

dan: agenda for the next 24h: finish all A/Bs, patch tool-field normalization, up soft-memory for critical shards ifneeded, and add warmup to boot process for dedicated pools. also add a regression test in CI that verifies identical fingerprint for semantically equivalent prompt shapes.

maria: agreed. i'll open a short-run incident doc with numbers and link to the dashboards.

nidhi: i'll PR the normalization and tokenizer pin flag.

jon: i'll schedule warmup rollout and add metrics alert: cache_hit_rate drop >5% sustained for 5m triggers paging.

maria: thanks everyone. big win — felt subtle at first but turned out to be a simple interaction (kernel mem footprint + prompt serialization quirk).

dan: lesson learned: coordinate kernel and prompt-builder changes in the same deploy window = bad signal hygiene :grimace:.

perf-bot: incident-note created: incident/2026-02-18/kv-eviction-spike (link)

maria: closing loop — will update this thread after E2 finishes (~2h). :eyes:
